newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals steady on limited arrivals, demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals steady on limited arrivals, demand.

text.p: Base metals were steady at the improved level on the local market on limited arrivals and restricted demand, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Fresh demand from industrial consumers remained restricted at the improved level but limited arrivals of imported metals kept prices around previous level," a dealer said.
Copper was steady at 13,450 rupees as was zinc at 7,700 rupees and tin at 31,500 rupees per quintal. On Tuesday copper and zinc were up 50 rupees each while tin rose 300 rupees.
Aluminium stood at the previous level of 7,500 rupees as was lead at 4,550 rupees and nickel at 37,300 rupees per quintal.

"Overall trading volume remained slow today but looking at the limited arrivals of imported metals as well as shortage of ready stock I am expecting base metals to move up in coming days on fresh buying support," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metals Exchange.
